chunks: And whatever is in it from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, I have narrated it from my father; and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdullah, and ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār and Aḥmad ibn Idrīs—may Allah be pleased with them—from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: may Allah be pleased with them both, an honorific supplication for two narrators
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ: may Allah be pleased with them, an honorific supplication for multiple narrators
key_terms.عَنْ أَبِي: from my father, one of the author's transmission authorities
key_terms.عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ: from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, indicating the point in the sanad/isnad being clarified
key_terms.فَقَدْ رَوَيْتُهُ: I have narrated it, indicating the author's direct transmission statement

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits narrations from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd. Its significance lies in documenting the transmission route in hadith literature and preserving the scholarly chain of authority.
